ev.q: During March 3–June 9, 2020, odds of SARS-CoV-2 infection in very high-deprivation areas of Utah were three times higher
Addresses were used to assign cases to one of 99 Utah small statistical areas
SARS-CoV-2 testing rates were calculated as the number of persons whose specimens were tested by real-time RT-PCR at least once per 100,000 persons.
Hospitalization rates were calculated as the number of patients with confirmed COVID-19 cases admitted to hospitals per 1,000 COVID-19 patients.
Percent positivity was calculated as the percentage of persons who received a positive SARS-CoV-2 test result among those tested.
Incidence of confirmed COVID-19 increased with area deprivation level, from 545 in very low-deprivation areas
Compared with persons living in very low-deprivation areas, age-weighted odds of having confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection were significantly higher
Age-weighted odds ratios (weighted ORs) were calculated by weighting rates for four age groups (≤24, 25–44, 45–64, and ≥65 years)
Area-level demographic and socioeconomic characteristics were also correlated with deprivation level
Addresses were used to assign cases to one of 99 Utah small statistical areas
Confirmed COVID-19 cases reported by local health departments and UDOH to the Utah National Electronic Disease Surveillance System

methods_quotes.q: Binary logistic regression was used to calculate unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) for incidence, hospitalization, and testing in each HII quintile
Rates for four age groups (≤24, 25–44, 25–64, and ≥65 years) were weighted to a U.S. Census 2000 age-standardized population
Weighted ORs were calculated by estimating the number of persons with the outcome of interest
Confidence intervals that do not span 1.0 are considered significant
